## Match imputation to the analysis

Default `mice` imputation in wsMed uses main effects of the raw variables.
Transforming completed data into difference scores and products does not make
that imputation model compatible with a moderated analysis. More imputations
reduce simulation error; they do not repair an incompatible conditional model.
Both interfaces now emit one `wsmed_mi_compatibility_warning` per internally
imputed fit with moderator interactions, even when the result is assigned
without printing it. The message remains in `wsmed_inspect(fit, "diagnostics")$warnings`
and the analysis manifest. External completions do not trigger this particular
warning; their compatibility still requires the imputer's own checks.

[Bartlett et al. (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1177/0962280214521348) describe
substantive-model-compatible fully conditional specification (SMC-FCS).
Here we use it to supply completed datasets to wsMed. The numerical pooling
and standardization procedure is the same as for internal imputation.

This worked example is deliberately limited: one mediator, observed moderator,
observed first-condition outcome and second-condition mediator, with a
normally distributed mediator conditional on its predictors. The first-condition
outcome is generated independently. This is **not** a general imputation recipe
for all within-subject models. In particular, missing values in both outcome
conditions, missing moderators, serial paths or extra auxiliary variables need
an appropriate joint/conditional model and their own validation.

Install the optional dependency with `install.packages("smcfcs")`.

## Generate the illustrative incomplete data


``` r
set.seed(720)
n <- 300
W <- rnorm(n)
A <- rnorm(n)
M <- .4 + .3*W + rnorm(n)
Y <- .2 + .1*W + (.4 + .2*W)*M + .2*A + rnorm(n)
y1 <- rnorm(n)
dat <- data.frame(y1, y2 = y1+Y, m1 = A-M/2, m2 = A+M/2, W)
dat$m1[runif(n) < .2] <- NA
dat$y2[runif(n) < .2] <- NA
model <- wsmed_model(c(before = "y1", after = "y2"),
  list(M = c(before = "m1", after = "m2")),
  moderator = list(variable = "W", interactions = "M -> Y"))
```

## Impute using the outcome interaction

Because y1 is observed, the outcome difference can be imputed and mapped back
to missing y2 values. The formula explicitly uses the mediator difference and
average; `I(m2-m1)*W` includes their difference slope, W and its interaction.
This avoids redundant columns when W is a factor. Product terms
are evaluated within the substantive model, not imputed as independent variables.
For this data-generating model, the imputation regression for m1 given m2 and W
is normal and linear. These are model assumptions, not data-validation results.


``` r
imp_data <- data.frame(yd = dat$y2-dat$y1, m1 = dat$m1, m2 = dat$m2, W = dat$W)
pred <- matrix(0, ncol(imp_data), ncol(imp_data),
  dimnames = list(names(imp_data), names(imp_data)))
pred["m1", c("m2", "W")] <- 1
set.seed(721)
imp <- withCallingHandlers(smcfcs::smcfcs(imp_data, smtype = "lm",
  smformula = "yd ~ I(m2-m1)*W + I((m1+m2)/2)",
  method = c("", "norm", "", ""), predictorMatrix = pred,
  m = 5, numit = 20, rjlimit = 5000), warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("Rejection sampling failed", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE))
      stop("Resolve the rejection-sampling warning before analysis: increase rjlimit, rerun imputation and review diagnostics.", call. = FALSE)
  })
#> [1] "Outcome variable(s): yd"
#> [1] "Passive variables: "
#> [1] "Partially obs. variables: m1"
#> [1] "Fully obs. substantive model variables: W"
#> [1] "Imputation  1"
#> [1] "Imputing missing outcomes using specified substantive model."
#> [1] "Imputing:  m1  using  m2,W  plus outcome"
#> [1] "Imputation  2"
#> [1] "Imputation  3"
#> [1] "Imputation  4"
#> [1] "Imputation  5"
completed <- lapply(imp$impDatasets, function(x) {
  d <- dat
  d$m1 <- x$m1
  missing_y <- is.na(dat$y2)
  d$y2[missing_y] <- dat$y1[missing_y]+x$yd[missing_y]
  d
})
```

Five imputations keep this tutorial short; choose the number of imputations and
iterations for the actual missing-information fraction and required precision.
Inspect `imp$smCoefIter` for mixing/stability and review rejection-sampling
warnings. The example stops on rejection-sampling failures; do not pass warned
imputations to the fitting step without resolving the issue. Twenty iterations
are an example setting, not a convergence guarantee.

The explicit predictor matrix matters: automatic predictor discovery in smcfcs
can miss m2 when it appears only inside `I(...)`. We specify the covariate model
`m1 ~ m2 + W`; the outcome is handled by the substantive-model step and must not
be added to that predictor matrix.

## Use either wsMed interface


``` r
fit <- wsmed_fit(model, dat, missing = "mi", mi = list(completed = completed))
inference <- wsmed_infer(fit, draws = 2000, seed = 722)
effects <- wsmed_effects(inference, at = list(W = c(-1, 0, 1)), scale = "marginal")
effects
#> wsMed indirect | marginal scale | mc 
#> 95% percentile intervals; 2000 joint draws; SE from effect draws
#> Condition contrast: after - before 
#> Moderator: W in raw units; centering reference = 0.00106494 
#> MI: per-imputation centering; first-imputation reporting reference.
#> External imputations: compatibility and convergence require the imputer's own checks. 
#> Standardization: effect / marginal model-implied SD(y2 - y1); condition contrast is unscaled.
#> Plug-in marginal outcome-difference SD: 1.16987 
#> The denominator is not a moderator-specific conditional SD.
#>                          Estimate Std. Error CI lower CI upper
#> indirect_1@1: M [W = -1]  0.04352    0.02870  0.00287  0.10946
#> indirect_1@2: M [W = 0]   0.17787    0.03456  0.11559  0.25144
#> indirect_1@3: M [W = 1]   0.40188    0.06618  0.28050  0.54041
#> Inference draws: 2000 retained of 2000 ; 0 excluded before effect extraction.
#> Use as.data.frame() for the full-precision table and metadata.

# The original one-call interface remains available.
one_call <- wsMed(dat, "m1", "m2", "y1", "y2", W = "W",
  MP = c("a1", "b1", "cp"), Na = "MI", R = 2000, standardized = TRUE,
  mi_args = list(completed = completed, seed = 722))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(coef(fit), coef(one_call$fit))))
```

The staged interface also accepts a `mice` mids object as `mi$completed`.
It infers m, validates row names/order, observed cells and factor levels, then
regenerates all differences, averages and products within each completed dataset.
It does not reimpute, and it cannot verify statistical compatibility from the
completed values alone. With the one-call interface, `mi_args$seed` still
controls MC; it does not describe the external imputation seed.

Save the external imputer object, its settings and package version separately
from the wsMed analysis manifest. The latter records that imputations were
external and their count, and deliberately excludes participant-level data.

## What the validation can establish

The development repository contains a paired study of the same incomplete
datasets analyzed with default PMM, SMC-FCS and the underlying complete data.
It records raw and standardized effects, estimated standardization denominators,
bias, coverage, simulation uncertainty, warnings and failures. This isolates the
effect of changing the imputer while keeping pooling and effect inference fixed.
See the [paired study report](https://github.com/Yangzhen1999/wsMed/blob/feature/modular-api/.github/validation/mi-comparison/RESULTS.md).

The comparison is restricted to its stated scenarios; it is not proof of nominal
coverage for arbitrary models, data distributions or missingness mechanisms.
